sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Intermodal ISO Shipping Container Fleet Asset Leasing

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (Grand Duchy of Luxembourg; unitary national jurisdiction)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg–China (PRC) Double Taxation Agreement (1979, as amended)
Luxembourg–United States Double Taxation Treaty and Protocol (1996, as amended 2009)
Luxembourg–France Double Taxation Agreement (1958, as amended)
EU–Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), applicable through EU membership
Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters (OECD/Council of Europe), in force for Luxembourg

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (notably by the Law of 25 March 2020 transposing Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs, RBE); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 14 January 2019 on the functioning of the RBE; CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended; Law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the valid passport of each director, shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority or competent notary public of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or current extract from the commercial register of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial registry or companies registrar of the shareholder's country of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Duly certified power of attorney for the incorporation process (procuration to the Luxembourg notary and counsel)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the country of origin or competent consular authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate resolution of the corporate shareholder approving the incorporation, capital subscription, and appointment of the initial manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or management body of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR certified notarial copy

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, and principal commercial counterparties against the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UN Security Council consolidated lists, OFAC SDN and SSI lists, and Luxembourg national restrictive measures maintained by the Ministry of Finance, together with PEP position checks applying CSSF criteria; enhanced due diligence is required for PEPs, high-risk third-country nationals, shell-bank nexus, and unexplained source of funds; screening results must be documented in the AML/CFT client file and retained for at least five years after the business relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RCSL — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés / Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) electronic portal (rcs.lbr.lu), with notarial electronic filing via MyGuichet.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Latin script; French is the working language of the RCSL; names in non-Latin scripts require a sworn transliteration into French, German, or Luxembourgish; the corporate name of a SARL must include the full form 'société à responsabilité limitée' or the abbreviation 'SARL'; the name must be lawful, distinctive, non-misleading, and must not contravene public order or good morals.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Luxembourg (when implying a State or public authority connection)
OPC / OPCVM / SICAV / Fonds d'investissement / Investment Fund
Prestataire de services de paiement / Payment Service Provider
Chambre de Commerce / Chamber of Commerce
Avocat / Notaire / Auditeur / Réviseur d'entreprises (reserved regulated liberal professions)
Grand-Ducal / Royal / Ministère / Administration (marks of sovereignty)
Any term requiring prior CSSF or ministerial approval or reserved to regulated professions by law
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a reasoned RCSL refusal, the applicant may (i) cure and re-file the name through the notary, (ii) request a formal written statement of reasons from the RCSL, and (iii) lodge an administrative appeal (recours en réformation) before the Administrative Tribunal of Luxembourg within three months of notification, in accordance with the Law of 7 November 1996 on the organization of administrative courts and administrative procedure; the statutory 30-day reservation window is not extendable, but re-filing without prejudice is permissible upon correction of the grounds for rejection.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the sole registered office. A SARL must maintain a physical registered office address in Luxembourg where the statutory records, minutes, and registers are kept and where legal process can be served; use of a licensed corporate domiciliation agent is acceptable where a genuine physical link, access, and substance are secured, but a fully virtual arrangement without any Luxembourg presence is inadmissible and would expose the entity to administrative dissolution, RCSL compliance challenges, and tax substance attack.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for routine years, estimated at approximately 5% annual probability for a non-regulated intermodal container leasing entity; the probability rises materially to approximately 15–25% in the presence of UBO inconsistencies, sanctions or PEP screening flags, atypical tax positioning, or if the registered office is a high-density domiciliation address identified by the authorities; on-site verification may be conducted by the RCSL, CSSF, social security authorities, and criminal investigatory bodies.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of incorporation (statuts) — drafting, execution and certification before a Luxembourg notary, including the mandatory statement of subscription and payment of the fully paid minimum SARL share capital of EUR 12,000
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg notary (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial tariff (tarif) plus fixed disbursements; prevailing benchmark EUR 1,500–2,000

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office domiciliation agreement — first annual fee with a licensed corporate domiciliation agent (physical office, statutory records storage, mail handling)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed corporate domiciliation agent in Luxembourg
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark EUR 1,500–2,500 per annum for commercial domiciliation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial register (RCSL) initial registration fee — filing of the articles of association and creation of the entity file
Publication of the incorporation instrument in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: RCSL (Ministry of Justice electronic publication service)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RBE (Register of Beneficial Owners) initial UBO filing — government-access-only disclosure of UBO data to the Luxembourg registries
Banker's certificate attesting the blocking of the fully subscribed share capital (attestation de blocage de fonds / certificate of capital availability) for the SARL's EUR 12,000 minimum capital
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg credit institution maintaining the blocked account
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark EUR 250–450 per certificate; may be waived or offset by the bank as a relationship incentive

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate counsel and incorporation services — legal due diligence, drafting of shareholder resolutions, manager appointment resolutions, AML/KYC file preparation, and filing coordination
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg law firm (avocat à la Cour)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market fixed or capped fee for a standard SARL incorporation scope (EUR 3,500–5,500)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT compliance and sanctions screening — automated PEP, OFAC, UN, EU, and national list screening of UBOs, directors, and counterparties, with source-of-funds verification files
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Law firm / licensed compliance screening provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per-name and per-entity screening tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and sworn translation of foreign corporate documents, powers of attorney, certificates of good standing, and passport copies
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent foreign authorities, Ministries of Foreign Affairs, accredited notaries, and Luxembourg sworn translators
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory apostille fees plus prevailing sworn translation per-page tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Ancillary administrative and contingency costs — e-Justice portal fees, certified extracts, courier, VAT on professional services where applicable, and general contingencies
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Disbursements and fixed contingency allowance; Luxembourg VAT at 17% applies where applicable

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), as amended; Articles 180-183 (constitution and minimum capital of the Société à Responsabilité Limitée) and Article 187 (management)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial Deed of Incorporation (Acte constitutif notarié) containing the Articles of Association (Statuts), filed with RCS Form A
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: EUR 12,000 statutory minimum share capital fully subscribed upon incorporation; at least 25% (EUR 3,000) must be paid up in cash at constitution and deposited into a blocked Luxembourg bank account evidenced by a bank blockage certificate (attestation de blocage) placed at the notary's disposal; the remaining 75% must be paid up within five years from incorporation; no additional state escrow requirement beyond the notarial deposit control
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the share capital of EUR 12,000, divided into one hundred twenty registered shares of EUR 100 each, is subscribed in full. RESOLVED, that the cash contributions are deposited and blocked with the designated Luxembourg credit institution, satisfying the statutory minimum paid-up capital requirement. RESOLVED, that the registered office is fixed at [registered office address], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg. RESOLVED, that [Name Surname] and [Name Surname] are appointed as co-managers (gérants), each acting alone. RESOLVED, that the managers are authorized to execute and file all documents for registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers, publication in the official gazette, and the business establishment permit application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Pre-Creation Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - RCS online name reservation portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to three proposed corporate names of the SARL for pre-registration verification. The name must not be contrary to public order and must be clearly distinguishable from all names already registered in the RCS. Obtain a name availability confirmation (certificat de non-confusion) to be presented to the notary and the bank.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name alternatives (up to three)
Passport copies of founding shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners
Brief description of the corporate purpose (container leasing and fleet management)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused due to confusion with an existing registered name, resubmit a new name request with distinctive additional elements such as activity descriptors or corporate suffixes; no administrative appeal is necessary where a new submission cures the objection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Share Capital Deposit and Bank Blockage Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (bank) or notarial escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account in the name of the SARL en formation; deposit at least EUR 3,000 being 25% of the EUR 12,000 minimum share capital in cash; obtain an attestation de blocage (blockage certificate) from the bank confirming that the amount is irrevocably held at the disposal of the notary; the funds may only be released upon presentation of the RCS registration certificate or the notary's written authorization.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association
Identity documents of the signatories
Source of funds documentation for the deposit
Signed bank account opening forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises AML/KYC objections, supplement the source of wealth evidence (bank statements, sale deeds, certified payroll records) or alternatively deposit the capital into a notarial escrow account with a Luxembourg notary to achieve the same legal effect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Notarial Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public (notaire) authorized to practice in Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before a Luxembourg notary with all founders; present the name availability certificate and the bank blockage certificate; execute the notarial deed of incorporation containing the full Articles of Association; the notary verifies the legality of the company purpose, the adequacy of the paid-up capital and the capacity of the appointed managers, then issues an authentic copy for RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Name availability certificate from LBR
Bank capital blockage certificate (attestation de blocage)
Passports and national identity cards of all shareholders and managers
Draft Articles of Association
Criminal record extracts (casier judiciaire) of the proposed managers, if available
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requires amendments to the draft articles for legal compliance, revise and resign the deed in a supplementary amending document; any founder who cannot appear personally may grant a notarized power of attorney to a Luxembourg-based representative.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Registration and Official Gazette Publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registration Department; electronic filing via LBR.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarial deed, RCS Form A (company particulars, registered office, managers' appointment and powers) and the financial declaration with the RCS electronically; complete the beneficial owner declaration (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs); pay the court registry fee; upon validation the company acquires legal personality and an RCS extract is issued; the RCS automatically transmits the incorporation notice for publication in the official electronic gazette (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations - RESA).
required_dossiers: Authentic notarial deed of incorporation
RCS Form A signed by the managers
Financial declaration (déclaration de constitution)
UBO declaration form for the Register of Beneficial Owners
Certified identification documents of managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct and resubmit any rectified forms objected to by the registrar within the statutory cure period (generally eight days); if the registry refuses registration, appeal against the refusal before the Luxembourg District Court within fifteen days of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Establishment Permit Application and Ancillary Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy - Direction de l'autorisation d'établissement; Administration de l'enregistrement et des domaines (AED) for VAT; Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the business establishment permit application (autorisation d'établissement) under the Law of 2 September 2011 regulating access to professions; demonstrate the professional qualification of the manager either by diploma or three years of relevant professional experience in transport equipment leasing; provide evidence of an administrative office and container storage or staging yard in Luxembourg; simultaneously register for VAT with the AED if taxable turnover is anticipated, and register the employer with the CCSS for social security.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract (extrait du registre de commerce)
Business establishment permit application form completed and signed
Identity document and criminal record extract of the manager
Professional qualification certificates or evidence of three years of professional experience
Lease agreement or title deed for the registered office and storage yard
Declaration of no outstanding tax or social security debts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the Ministry of the Economy's completeness objections within fifteen days; upon refusal, appeal before the Administrative Tribunal within three months of notification, or file a request for interim suspension if the denial causes irreparable harm to the operational launch.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy - Business Establishment Department (Direction de l'autorisation d'établissement)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C - no full EIA required; container leasing (ISIC 5229) is not listed in Annexes I or II of the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment; only a prior administrative declaration is triggered where ancillary container storage covers more than 5,000 square metres of gross footprint or involves coating, fumigation or heavy washing operations, in which case a simplified registration dossier must be filed with the Administration de l'environnement
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or VOC point sources expected; all sanitary wastewater must meet communal discharge standards (BOD5 below 20 mg/L and TSS below 30 mg/L for sanitary flows under 500 cubic metres per year); any incidental anti-corrosion coating repairs must use low-VOC paints (VOC content under 300 g/L) and remain below the 2 tonnes per year reporting threshold; damaged containers must be handled as ferrous metal waste (EWC 17 04 05) and transferred to a licensed waste collector pursuant to the Law of 21 March 2017 on waste prevention and management

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance for the office premises from the competent communal fire prevention authority, including certificates for fire extinguishers, emergency lighting and evacuation plan; structural load inspection by an approved engineer for any container stacking configured above two tiers; workplace clearance from the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) covering access routes, sanitary facilities, ventilation, adequate lighting and first-aid equipment as required under the amended Luxembourg Labor Code and the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 17 November 2004 on workplace safety

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT, registration duties and excise; Administration des douanes et accises (Luxembourg Customs and Excise Agency) for customs export procedures and EORI; single national e-government portal: MyGuichet.lu (RCS/LBR corporate filings, AEDT VAT filing, VIES recapitulative statements, SAF-T submissions, customs ECS declarations).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Execute notarial deed of incorporation and deposit it with the RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) via the Luxembourg Business Registers electronic portal on MyGuichet.lu; the RCS assigns a 13-digit national identification number (numéro d'identification / matricule) which automatically serves as the corporate tax reference for the ACD, with no separate ACD application required. Step 2: File Form 640 (declaration d'inscription à la TVA) with the AEDT before commencing taxable activity; the AEDT issues an 8-digit VAT identification number with the LU prefix (format LU + 8 digits) and coordinates with customs for EORI issuance (the VAT number generally functions as the EORI). Step 3: Register all beneficial owners in the RBE (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) within one month of incorporation, with penalties for late filing. Step 4: Non-resident companies without a Luxembourg fixed establishment but making taxable supplies in Luxembourg must register directly with the AEDT under the simplified non-established VAT registration procedure, submitting proof of foreign VAT ID, constitutional documents, foreign register excerpt and director identification; no notarisation is required for the VAT-only registration. Step 5: For the ISO container leasing SARL, the LU VAT ID covers intra-Community supplies (EC Sales List filings), export declarations via ECS, and supplier verification under the reverse-charge mechanism.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not apply a US-style check-the-box regime; classification follows statutory legal form. A SARL is a resident capital company subject to entity-level corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax if its registered office (siège statutaire) or central administration (direction effective) is in Luxembourg; worldwide income is taxed with territorial exemptions for foreign permanent establishments and for qualifying participations (participation exemption, Article 166 LIR). Available elections: (1) fiscal unity / integrated taxation under Article 164bis LIR for 99%+ owned resident group members (CIT and municipal business tax consolidation); (2) VAT grouping election under Article 60 LTVA creating a single taxable person for financially, economically and organisationally linked entities; (3) waiver of the small-enterprise VAT exemption under Article 57 LTVA; (4) advance tax ruling application to the ACD confirming tax classification and indirect tax treatment of the container leasing model; (5) IP box election under Article 50bis LIR for qualifying intellectual property income; (6) exit tax deferral election under Article 111 LIR; (7) no hybrid mismatch election is available — anti-hybrid rules under Article 168quater LIR (ATAD 1 and 2) and the general anti-abuse rule under Article 6a LIR override contractual classifications that result in deduction/non-inclusion mismatches.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée - TVA) under the Luxembourg VAT Law (Loi TVA, implementing EU Directive 2006/112/EC); no separate sales and use tax; no sub-jurisdictional VAT variation within the unitary national system.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general registration threshold for established suppliers: any business supplying taxable goods or services in Luxembourg must register unless covered by the small-enterprise exemption. Small-enterprise exemption threshold: EUR 35,000 annual turnover (Article 57 LTVA); crossing the threshold or voluntarily waiving the exemption triggers VAT registration. Intra-EU distance sales of goods and remote B2C services: EUR 10,000 annual cross-border turnover threshold per Member State under the Union scheme; above this threshold, Luxembourg VAT registration is mandatory. Non-established suppliers of B2C services and electronically supplied services have zero registration threshold and must register from the first euro.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg has no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or digital stamping regime. E-invoicing is voluntary for B2B and B2C; every invoice must guarantee authenticity of origin, integrity of content and legibility (Article 84 LTVA) via audit trail, EDI or electronic signature. Mandatory structured e-invoicing applies only to B2G public procurement supplies, with contracting authorities obliged to receive PEPPOL BIS 3.0 e-invoices; supplier-side B2G e-invoicing is being phased in. SAF-T-LUX (fichier d'écritures comptables) is the statutory VAT audit file; its electronic transmission to the AEDT is progressively mandatory: large taxpayers from 1 January 2023, mid-size taxpayers from 1 January 2025, with extension to all VAT payers in subsequent phases. The EU ViDA reform is expected to introduce mandatory structured e-invoicing for cross-border B2B supplies from 2030, with domestic B2B mandates thereafter.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of physical goods to non-EU destinations (Article 43 LTVA): zero-rated where the ISO containers are exported from EU customs territory and the supplier holds proof of export showing the goods left the EU within 90 days of supply. Intra-Community supplies (Article 44 LTVA): zero-rated as exempt with deduction where containers are dispatched to a customer in another Member State, the customer's valid VAT ID is confirmed via VIES, the EC Sales List/recapitulative statement is filed, and transport documents evidence the movement. For cross-border container box leasing, which is by law a supply of services (hire of goods), the bare lease does not qualify for export zero-rating; the general B2B place-of-supply rule (Article 15 LTVA) locates the supply where the customer is established, leaving the lease outside Luxembourg VAT and subject to reverse charge in the customer's jurisdiction, subject to documentary evidence of customer business status and VAT ID. Services directly linked to international maritime transport of goods, including certain container handling and inland legs aggregated to a definite shipping voyage, may qualify for exemption with deduction under Articles 50 and 51 LTVA; given case-law sensitivity, an advance VAT ruling from the AEDT is recommended to secure the treatment of the specific leasing contract.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (SAD/EXA filed through the ECS electronic system, including the Movement Reference Number) issued by Luxembourg Customs and Excise Agency
Bill of Lading, sea waybill, CMR or Air Waybill proving physical departure of the containers from EU customs territory
Inward Remittance Certificate (SWIFT/bank credit advice) evidencing settlement of the export transaction and traceability of foreign currency proceeds to the SARL's Luxembourg bank account
Commercial invoice and executed lease agreement identifying the customer, the container population, lease term and consideration
VIES validation certificate and VAT ID of the EU customer for intra-Community zero-rated supplies
Packing list, container inspection/survey report and handover protocol
Freight forwarder or shipping line certificate of export confirming destination port and date of departure
Filing confirmation of the EC Sales List (recapitulative statement) and Intrastat declaration where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEDT and customs jointly audit zero-rating claims against the complete documentary bundle; missing or inconsistent export evidence triggers retrospective reassessment of output VAT, denial of corresponding input VAT deduction, statutory interest on arrears at 0.8% per month (9.6% annualised), and administrative fines of up to EUR 2,500 per infraction under the VAT Law. In cases of forged export documents, circular transactions, or artificial arrangements lacking economic substance, the GAAR (Article 6a LIR) and VAT anti-abuse rules apply, exposing the SARL to criminal tax fraud penalties under the criminal provisions of the VAT Law and the Criminal Code: imprisonment ranging from 8 days to 5 years and/or fines from EUR 250 to EUR 50,000, publication of sanctions, exclusion from the deduction of input VAT, and extension of the audit and clawback period to 10 years. Standard reassessment remains possible for 5 years from the end of the declaration year.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) acting in coordination with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for financial sector supervision and payment systems oversight; no separate foreign exchange administration exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg maintains full convertibility of the euro for both current and capital account transactions, reflecting EU Treaty obligations on free movement of capital. There are no approval requirements for cross-border payments, no exchange control surrender requirements, and no restrictions on foreign currency accounts. Profit remittance by a Luxembourg SARL is structurally unimpeded from an FX perspective; distributable profits may be transferred abroad net of any applicable Luxembourg withholding tax on dividends. The 15% normal withholding tax on dividends is reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or Luxembourg domestic participation exemption rules, and to 5% or 0% under applicable tax treaties, provided the documentary thresholds are satisfied.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no prescribed repatriation timeline for export receipts. Invoice settlement may be retained in EUR or any freely negotiated foreign currency. The only legal obligations concern record-keeping under commercial law, tax documentation, and anti-money laundering / sanctions screening under EU regulations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility. EU-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) and payment institutions holding a MiFID / API passport may provide euro IBAN accounts and cross-border payment connectivity to a Luxembourg SARL. However, such arrangements are typically inferior to bank credit lines, are often rejected for escrow or capital-subscription deposits because they do not satisfy all notarial evidence chains, and may trigger enhanced scrutiny where EMIs rely on distributed agent networks. A Luxembourg SARL engaged in physical container leasing should maintain at least one tier-1 Luxembourg bank account or an EU branch of a credit institution authorised by the BCL/CSSF for core treasury operations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors of a Luxembourg SARL must, in practice, attend either an in-person onboarding meeting at the bank’s registered office or, in the case of remote digital onboarding, a live videoconference interview before the bank's compliance officer. Physical presence is not always statutorily mandated, but CSSF-guided AML policies at most tier-1 banks require a face-to-face or real-time audiovisual identification for a non-resident director and for any beneficial owner holding more than 25% of shares. The ultimate beneficial owner(s) and the authorised signatory must present valid passports, proof of address, professional background, and source-of-funds evidence. A notarised power of attorney may be used but does not waive the director’s obligation to be identified.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident corporate shareholder located in a jurisdiction with no direct EU tax-information exchange agreement or listed as high-risk under FATF.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a complete chain of corporate ownership, certified articles of incorporation and registration excerpts, tax residency certificate, audited financial statements or management accounts showing legitimate source of funds, and legal opinion confirming the corporate structure was not designed for tax evasion, together with a detailed explanation for the geographic settlement route.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained high-frequency or unusually structured third-party payments, particularly from countries that are not counterparties to the container leasing activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply commercial contracts, invoices, container lease agreements, bill-of-lading or terminal receipts, inspection certificates, a list of counterparties with KYC documents, and the treasury payment matrix demonstrating that transaction volumes and frequencies match the operational leasing portfolio.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Leveraged capital structure with shareholder loans, especially where a Luxembourg SARL receives intercompany funding shortly after incorporation and simultaneously makes large upstream payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare notarised loan agreements, board resolutions authorising the funding, interest-rate and transfer-pricing documentation, updated cash-flow projections, and evidence that the borrower’s capacity to repay is supported by binding container lease contracts and independent third-party valuation of the container fleet assets.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of offshore bank accounts, shell companies, or EMIs with opaque ownership for the collection of lease income.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Restructure all revenue receipts to be routed through the Luxembourg operating account or a fully transparency-compliant EU bank account; additionally provide corporate charts, ultimate beneficial owner declarations, and the tax registration documents of all subsidiaries and trading partners.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity contributions to a Luxembourg SARL must be wired from the shareholder’s verified bank account via SWIFT MT103 to the company’s dedicated capital account at a Luxembourg credit institution. The wire instruction must include a clear purpose code reflecting 'Shareholders’ equity contribution' and, where applicable, the name of the company and the deed reference. For bank compliance, provide the notarised incorporation deed or deed of amendment evidencing the share capital increase, share subscription forms, and proof of identity of the fund remitter. Beneficiary accounts should be blocked for operational drawdowns until the notarial capital verification certificate has been obtained and any statutory publication has been made in the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register. Inbound loans should be documented by a formal loan agreement and routed through the same compliant banking network using an intercompany loan purpose code.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Container purchases and operating expenses are paid using standard SWIFT MT103 customer credits for single payments, while SWIFT MT202 or MT202 COV may be used for interbank cover or high-value transfers between financial institutions. Trade-related settlements with container manufacturers and stevedores can be executed via irrevocable commercial letters of credit, documentary collection, or open account with purchase-order support. The Luxembourg SARL may also use electronic payments through TARGET2 and SEPA INST for euro-based operational disbursements; for non-euro counterparties, a dual-currency settlement structure should be established to maximise payment efficiency. All outbound transmissions should include the supporting invoice and lease contract references in the free-format fields to ensure unaudited traceability.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forward Contracts concluded with a Luxembourg or EU-authorised credit institution
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for emerging-market currencies, subject to bank-counterparty approval and ISDA documentation
Cross-Currency Swaps for financing currencies and periodic swap of principal and interest
FX Options (plain vanilla put and call options) for corridor hedging of lease receivables
Currency swaps with the bank for project-level re-financing of container fleet assets

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual accounts (annee comptable) with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR/RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after financial year-end, i.e., by 30 June for a calendar-year company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court order for late filing; administrative fine up to EUR 5,000; possible criminal sanction for directors

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% national corporate income tax (Impôt sur le Revenu des Collectivités) plus 7% solidarity surcharge (Contribution de Solidarité) plus municipal business tax (Impôt Commercial Communal, 6.75% in Luxembourg City), yielding aggregate headline rate of 24.94% for Luxembourg City
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday for container leasing; applicable incentives include participation exemption for qualifying dividend and capital gains (100% exempt if 10% holding and holding period > 12 months), IP box with 80% exemption for qualifying IP income, investment tax credits under LIR Art. 152bis for certain capital expenditures, and notional interest deduction for qualifying new equity

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 500 and Form 500-A (Déclaration pour l’impôt sur les sociétés) filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu / eSpace portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing must occur by 31 May of the year following the fiscal year-end; automatic extension may be applied for online, usually to 31 December of the same year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax identification and entity profile: RNE registration number, name, legal form (SARL), registered office address, date of incorporation, corporate purpose
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert Luxembourg RNE number and registered address; confirm central administration and effective management in Luxembourg to support tax residency of the SARL; do not claim residency solely from registered office if management occurs abroad.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period, applied accounting framework (Lux GAAP / IFRS optional), reporting currency
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the same financial year as the statutory accounts; if accounts are maintained in a foreign currency, state the relevant conversion method consistent with Luxembourg accounting and tax rules; IRS-recognized conversion for CTI purposes must be volume-weighted average or year-end rate per Luxembourg tax practice.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computation: gross leasing revenues, container deprecation at prescribed USASC/asset-life rates under Article 23 LIR, interest expense cap, capital allowances, taxable reserves
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Luxembourg-resident SARL, worldwide taxable income must be declared; include all ISO container lease rentals and ancillary logistics services; attach intercompany lease agreements and a transfer pricing file sufficiently identifying fleet allocation, buy-sell marks, residual value risk, and finance terms.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss compensation and tax attributes, including prior year available losses and net wealth tax (Impôt sur la Fortune) adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses generated under Luxembourg tax recognition are deductible; lost-carryforward is limited to 5 years from the loss year; associate the return with a loss carryforward statement to substantiate position before an auditor.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: mandatory 10% penalty (majoration d’impôt) on assessed tax; late-payment surcharge interest of 0.8% per month on tax due; gross negligence may increase penalty to 50%; willful tax fraud criminal fines of €10,000 to €50,000 and imprisonment; arbitrary assessment by tax authority may estimate income at 150% of declared prior-year income if return is not filed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 700 (Declaration for municipal business tax) and Form 507 (Net wealth tax return), filed alongside the annual CIT return through MyGuichet.lu
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Same statutory deadline as CIT return: 31 May following year-end; deferral to 31 December possible on online extension.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Municipal business tax computation base, including the container leasing trade profits allocated to the Luxembourg permanent establishment
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Luxembourg SARL, all domestic profits from container lease management, fleet storage, and related services are subject to Luxembourg municipal business tax; if the operational container fleet is located abroad, ensure proper profit attribution under transfer-pricing rules does not convert into an unintended foreign PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net wealth tax taxable capital: container assets (net of statutory depreciation), related-party loans, shareholdings, net of qualifying liabilities
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an LRPL (Luxembourg Risk Premium Lease) structure, state the container fleet at net carrying value; for non-resident shareholders, net wealth tax is assessed at 0.5% rate; minimum contribution of €3,595 per year applies to SARLs if rebased.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties mirror the CIT regime: 10% forced penalty, 0.8% monthly late interest, and potential reassessment of municipal business tax base; missed net-wealth declarations also trigger the automatic minimum tax assessment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% on gross dividends paid by a Luxembourg resident SARL; reduced to 0% in qualifying EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive scenarios and tax treaty cases where exemption or zero rate is available (e.g., dividends to Swiss resident parent under applicable protocols may be subject 0% or 5%)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Claim must be lodged with the Luxembourg Administration des contributions directes (ACD) through MyGuichet or via tax return; applicant must submit a valid tax residency certificate (TRC/Formulaire 5) issued by the recipient state tax authority, evidence of beneficial ownership, a shareholding history (10% or more, holding period), and relevant DTA article; EU Directive relief is automatic only after a prior authorization obtained by applying any Luxembourg tax circular with Form 1-EU; refund claims must be filed within the legal limitation period of six months after the dividend date.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg has no withholding tax on outgoing royalties and outgoing interest (statutory rate 0%); under extensive DTA network treaty rates are generally 0% for interest and royalties, but the beneficial ownership requirement and Luxembourg substance conditions must be met; high interest payments to hybrid mismatches may be denied deduction under ATAD and Luxembourg interest barriers under §50stany (Luxeuro-Riotry law)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Country-by-Country Report threshold is EUR 750,000,000 consolidated group revenue; Luxembourg statutory local-file/master-file requirements apply when the taxpayer either exceeds EUR 3,000,000 aggregate intercompany transactions during a fiscal year or is part of a group with EUR 50,000,000 aggregated net turnover; container-leasing fees, fleet management fees, and financing transactions are deemed controlled transactions and must be documented contemporaneously; smaller SARLs must still keep sufficient documentation upon request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not maintain a formal statutory Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) equivalent UAE-style, but an economic substance requirement is applied through the EU ATAD anti-abuse articles (Article 6, 60ter LIR), the Shell Company Act of 2023, DTA limitation-of-benefit clauses and administrative practice: an SARL leasing ISO containers in Luxembourg must demonstrate actual decision-making, management staff, physical office space, aggregation of container fleet in tax records, and operational supervision; absence of substance will trigger treaty denial, dividend withholding at statutory 15%, potential recharacterization of transactions, and administrative penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion - Fraudulent Understatement of CIT
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of container lease income, hidden intercompany rentals, deliberate defective invoicing to sister entities, or artificial transfer of container revenue to a no-substance offshore affiliate
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of evaded tax plus penalty of up to 150% of omitted tax (majoration pour manœuvre frauduleuse); criminal fine of €10,000 to €50,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years; publication of the sanction by the Luxembourg direct tax administration in cases of serious recidivism
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for the tax debt where they signed the false return, committed fraud not attributable to the company, or stripped the SARL of assets; statutory liability under Article 1851 Civil Code and LIR Art. 62 (veil piercing); travel bans and detention pending criminal prosecution; civil restitution to the tax authority of the evaded taxes plus interest.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Artificial Substance Abusive Arrangement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Luxembourg SARL has no real office, no independent management, no paid employees, no ownership-retained risk of container fleet, leases containers solely as a pass-through conduit to related enterprises, and carries no local decisions regarding fleet acquisition or lease terms
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of corporate tax losses and treaty benefits under the Shell Company Act of 29 December 2023; application of Article 6 ATAD: minimum of 15% withholding recovered at source; reclassification of the SARL as transparent for tax purposes; revocation of advance tax rulings; fines for tax avoidance up to €30,000 and possible commercial deregistration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors may be personally assessed for unpaid withholding taxes if the company lacks substance; civil liability for orchestrating an artificial arrangement arises under general tort law; managers may face travel restrictions and enforcement proceedings under the 2018 EU Mutual Recovery Directive.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The SARL charges non-arm’s-length container rental rates to foreign related parties, inflates management fees from a connected services entity, retains no evidence of the fleet’s capacity, does not prepare a TP file or master/local file before deadline, or fails to disclose related-party transaction on tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: An upward tax adjustment restating taxable income at arm’s length; penalty of 25% of the additional tax paid for grossly negligent TP documentation (Art. 100 StAnp/LIR); possible secondary adjustment and deemed dividends; interest of 0.8% per month on underpaid CIT until settlement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the SARL who knowingly approved inaccurate intercompany pricing are jointly and severally liable for the company’s unpaid tax liabilities; penalties against directors under Luxembourg tax law can be up to €20,000; court-ordered restitution of benefit obtained by the related party may be sought and personal bankruptcy for unpaid debt if fraud driving the TP file is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Entering into container-leasing transactions with undisclosed UBOs, failing to register the ultimate shareholders in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), accepting payments through unverified third-party bank account structures, or allowing cash settlement above €10,000 without AML due diligence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Post-BRED-actuary enforcement: administrative fines up to €1,250,000; criminal penalties of imprisonment for 6 months to 5 years; immediate suspension of the SARL’s right to hold bank accounts; forfeiture of container assets used in the offence; CSSF will issue a formal notice and sanctions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Each director and effective manager may be individually criminally prosecuted for AML failures; personal fines up to €2,500,000 for entities, shareholders may be ordered to disgorge profits; travel bans and extradition risk if criminal laundering is proved; personal bankruptcy upon civil judgment for damages to third-party creditors.
